added_claims.speaker: Nick Baltas

added_claims.claim: Commodity curve carry (long the back end, short the front) has historically been rewarded because it earns a risk premium shared between commodity consumers and producers, which is why its drawdowns tend to be temporary unless the supply shock is permanent.
added_claims.indicator: commodity futures curve carry (back vs front)
added_claims.direction: long deferred contracts, short front contracts
added_claims.conditions: fails when backwardation persists, e.g. supply shock or weather shock

added_claims.quote: then you realize that doing it on the front has a negative roll yield. You do it on the back end of the curve, you realize you have some alpha, you short the front, here's your curve.

added_claims.direction: long back / short front of commodity curve

corrections.issue: Attribution overstated. Nick hedged that he might misrepresent the paper and said the dealer-long-gamma finding supports more short-term reversals than intraday trends; the link to weak short-term trend performance was Niels's own suggestion, with Nick saying 0DTE is 'certainly a force' but not that it is proven.
corrections.fix: A study (attributed with hedging to Greg Vilkov and co-authors) finds dealers are typically more long gamma than short gamma, implying more intraday reversals than trends; Niels then suggests this may help explain weak short-term trend results recently, which Nick treats as plausible but unproven.
